same_child_directed_scenario_range_q95_q.interpretation: Scenario envelope for the quantified trust-excluded child-directed alternatives using q95 or q99, not an uncertainty interval; the q100+ terminal mapping is shown separately as an extreme mechanical sensitivity.

scenarios.interpretation: Published elements: 25% married-head death; 75% otherwise; trust-excluded estate proxy; aggregate net-worth denominator. Assumed: head qx applied to whole PEU estate; legal marital status; qx95; shares applied to every PEU because lifetime-child status is unavailable.

Published 25%/75% child shares retained. Assumed: independent spouse deaths, half of PEU wealth attributed to a single spouse death, full wealth at joint death; no SCF ownership evidence supports this allocation.

scenarios.estimand_class: Same child-directed estimand; partner-recipient mapping alternative
scenarios.interpretation: Only change: SCF living-with-partner households receive the 25% share as married households. This legal/cohabiting mapping is not resolved by the published description.
Only change: every SCF age top-coded at 95 maps to NCHS qx99; mechanical age mapping, not an uncertainty interval.

scenarios.estimand_class: Same child-directed estimand; terminal mortality mapping
scenarios.interpretation: Only change: every SCF age top-coded at 95 maps to terminal NCHS 100+ qx=1.0; extreme mechanical sensitivity, not a plausible point estimate or uncertainty bound.
Only change: include trust assets in positive estate base; denominator remains aggregate signed NETWORTH. This departs from GS trust-excluded numerator treatment.
Only change: denominator becomes aggregate signed NETWORTH-TRUSTS rather than aggregate NETWORTH. This changes the published denominator concept.

This removes the child shares and measures gross modeled estate leaving decedent ownership under equal-split/independent-death assumptions. Not a robustness estimate of the adopted child-directed moment.

scenarios.estimand_class: Child-directed eligibility: not quantifiable from saved data
scenarios.interpretation: SCF KIDS counts currently rostered natural/step/foster children, not all living offspring or lifetime child status. No valid saved alternative eligibility measure; no numeric sensitivity reported.

equations.adopted_ratio: sum_i WGT_i * qx(head age, head sex) * alpha_i * max(NETWORTH_i-TRUSTS_i,0) / sum_i WGT_i * NETWORTH_i, with WGT=X42001/5 across all five implicates; alpha=.25 for legally married SCF head and .75 otherwise.
equations.spouse_alternative: For married couples assume independent deaths: P(one)=qh*(1-qs)+qs*(1-qh), P(both)=qh*qs; assign half PEU estate to one decedent and all to joint death, then apply .25 and .75 child shares respectively. Singles use .75*qh*estate.
equations.interpretive_guardrail: All-estate transfer excludes recipient shares and is a different estimand. Scenario differences are sensitivity analyses, not sampling uncertainty.

main_result: Among quantified same-child-directed alternatives, spouse death/wealth allocation has the largest q95 change (equal-split independent-spouse scenario: -0.0666598829568844 percentage points). Mapping all 95+ observations to terminal q100+ raises the ratio by 0.0534910042131592 points; this is an extreme mapping. Child eligibility cannot be quantified from KIDS.

source_basis.scenario_grid: scenario_estimates.csv (saved 72-row computation; no raw SCF rebuild)
source_basis.published_conventions: GS 1993 IRP pp. 12-14: trust/pension treatment and 25%/75% child shares; marital estate ownership at one-spouse vs joint death and lifetime-child eligibility are undocumented in reviewed sources.
